core.title: Assess every route category of an interlocking
core.given: An interlocking in the plan; its route space is the closed category set nominal, alternate, error, exception
core.when: The plan is assessed at CONFIRM (every interlocking, changed or not)
core.then: Assess every category explicitly: nominal carries one or more routes, and alternate, error and exception each carry routes or a typed not-applicable basis from the closed vocabulary.
prefer: For alternate, error and exception, state what happens: write the routes or pick the matching closed-vocabulary basis
Ensure that, as assessed at CONFIRM, no category carries both routes and a not-applicable basis
avoid: One token alternate route while error and exception stay unwritten
Declaring nominal not-applicable (it is the executed path)
A not-applicable basis on a category that carries routes (stale contradiction)
core.why: 'At least one non-nominal route' is gamed by a token alternate; assessing each category forces stating what happens on each, and a typed not-applicable stops the escape eroding into copy-pasted prose.
evidence: The route-category assessment check passes in CONFIRM

For each interlocking, every category of {nominal, alternate, error, exception} has an assessment status; nominal has >=1 route; each other category has routes or a closed-vocabulary not-applicable basis, never both
verification: A presence-style check over the plan model: the category space is closed (nominal, alternate, error, exception); a missing category is a finding
nominal requires at least one route; nominal is the executed path, so any not-applicable basis on nominal is a finding

alternate/error/exception each pass iff routes are present XOR a not-applicable basis is present; the basis must be a member of the closed vocabulary (free prose is a finding); routes and basis together is a contradiction finding (prevents stale assessments)
Runs at CONFIRM and is confirm-blocking; it assesses every interlocking in the plan regardless of whether it changed
A finding reports the interlocking, the affected category, its routes, any not-applicable basis, and the assessment status
The members of the closed not-applicable vocabulary are not enumerated in this rule; the checker's accepted basis list is authoritative
The check enumerates its interlocking subjects from the plan model; no file-level identification of subjects is established, so an observer must derive subjects from the plan

fires: At CONFIRM, an interlocking has only nominal routes and leaves alternate, error and exception unaddressed
At CONFIRM, an existing interlocking that was not edited in this change still lacks an assessment for error or exception
An interlocking has a nominal route plus one token alternate route while error and exception have neither routes nor a typed not-applicable basis
An interlocking marks error as not-applicable using free prose instead of a basis from the closed vocabulary
An interlocking marks a category not-applicable while that category already carries routes
An interlocking declares nominal as not-applicable
doesNotFire: At CONFIRM, every interlocking has nominal routes and alternate, error and exception each have routes or a typed not-applicable basis, with no category both routed and marked not-applicable
Phases other than CONFIRM, e.g. drafting unrelated plan documents — but any invalid interlocking, edited or not, still fails once the plan reaches CONFIRM

neutralityNotes: This convention is a plan-model rule about the planning domain (interlocking route categories), so its substance was already stack-neutral: no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path appears in given/when/then/prefer/avoid/why, and nothing concrete is needed from the structure profile (profileRequirements empty; the subject is enumerated from the plan model, not identified by file kind, so roles.plan_artifact.kinds is not required). CONFIRM and the category names nominal/alternate/error/exception are planning-method vocabulary, not stack specifics, and are kept verbatim. The closed not-applicable basis vocabulary is owned by the checker, not the structure profile, so its enumeration is deferred in core:verification to the checker's accepted basis list. The only Bun-specific content is this rule's realization identifiers: the validator test id (evidence[0]), the family/template/variant registry triple (verifier_detail[3]) and the failure_evidence field names (verifier_detail[4]); all are bunOnly, with neutral equivalents in core:evidence and core:verification. The activation facts' explanatory notes were folded into core:verification rather than dropped.
